title: Loading and Error States knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Loading and Error States”?
options: Loading and Error States helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Loading and Error States means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Loading and Error States removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Loading and Error States should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Loading and Error States helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Loading and Error States is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Loading indicators” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Loading indicators” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Loading indicators” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Loading indicators” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Loading indicators” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Loading indicators” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Loading indicators” under Loading and Error States. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Loading and Error States”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
